args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN DEVIATION REPORT
Bankruptcy Restructuring — Committee Redlined Plan vs. Debtor's Original Plan of Reorganization

Prepared by: Law Firm Company
Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Engagement: Compare the committee's redlined plan against the debtor's original plan, using the attached valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts, and prepare a deviation report.

---

I. SCOPE AND SOURCES

This deviation report reconciles the committee's redlined plan of reorganization (the "Committee Plan") against the debtor's original plan of reorganization (the "Debtor's Plan" or "Base Plan"). The analysis is grounded in the following source materials:

1. Debtor's Original Plan of Reorganization (base materials) — containing representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions negotiated between the parties.
2. Committee's Redlined Plan (counterparty markup) — the working revision circulated by the committee for review.
3. Valuation Summary (attached to the matter) — referenced in the engagement instruction as supporting evidence for economic positions.
4. Transmittal Email (attached to the matter) — referenced in the engagement instruction as conveying the committee's revisions.
5. Disclosure Statement Excerpts (attached to the matter) — referenced in the engagement instruction as describing the reorganization relative to the operative schedules and exhibits.
6. Schedules and Exhibits — Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix), which qualify the Debtor's Plan.
7. Deal Correspondence — partner email thread containing the controlling instruction on negotiating priorities.

The scheduled exceptions set forth in Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B control over any general statements in the base materials. The independently identified deviations in the Committee Plan have been evaluated against these schedules and exhibits, and against the controlling deal team instruction.

---

II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Committee Plan accepts most of the Debtor's Plan provisions but introduces three material deviations that must be reconciled:

Deviation 1 — Indemnification: The indemnification cap is silently reduced from the Debtor's Plan level, and the indemnity basket is converted from a deductible structure to a tipping basket structure.

Deviation 2 — Material Adverse Effect (MAE): The definition of MAE is expanded to add carve-outs for regulatory action of precisely the kind at issue in this restructuring.

Deviation 3 — Survival Period: A new limitation period is introduced that shortens the survival of the core representations relative to Exhibit B of the Debtor's Plan.

Each deviation is analyzed below against the relevant schedule/exhibit, the applicable valuation context, and the controlling deal team instruction.

---

III. DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP AND INDEMNITY BASKET

A. Description of the Deviation

In the Committee Plan, the indemnification cap is silently reduced relative to the Debtor's Plan. In addition, the indemnity basket — the threshold that must be reached before indemnification claims can be made — is converted from a deductible basket (under which the indemnitor is responsible for the full amount of all claims once the threshold is crossed) to a tipping basket (under which the indemnitor is responsible only for amounts in excess of the threshold once it is satisfied).

B. Interaction with Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities)

Schedule 5.2 of the Debtor's Plan lists retained liabilities that the indemnification provisions were intended to cover. Under the Debtor's Plan, these retained liabilities were allocated to the estate and any post-confirmation claims associated with them were intended to be addressed through the indemnification regime at the negotiated cap and through a deductible basket structure.

The Committee Plan's changes operate in tandem: (i) the reduced cap decreases the maximum aggregate exposure available for claims arising from the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, and (ii) the conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket shifts the economic burden so that losses below the threshold are borne entirely by the estate/claimants, with the indemnitor only paying amounts in excess of the threshold. Combined, these changes materially reduce the committee's recovery protection for Schedule 5.2 liabilities.

C. Valuation Assessment

The attached valuation summary confirms that a material portion of the projected reorganization value is allocated to cover the retained liabilities listed in Schedule 5.2. Reducing the indemnification cap while simultaneously converting the basket to a tipping structure would, in the aggregate, shift meaningful value away from the estate's creditors and toward the debtor. Under the valuation assumptions in the Debtor's Plan, the retained liabilities constitute a significant component of the claims pool; the Committee Plan's changes understate the true risk exposure associated with those liabilities.

D. Negotiating Position

Per the controlling deal correspondence, the client has decided to concede the basket conversion (i.e., from deductible to tipping basket). This is a negotiated concession that the client is willing to accept. Accordingly, the firm should not resist the tipping basket conversion as a standalone point.

However, the reduction of the indemnification cap is not conceded and should be resisted. The cap reduction, combined with the tipping basket, operates to further diminish the protection available for Schedule 5.2 liabilities. The client should push back on the reduced cap and seek to restore the indemnification cap to the level set forth in the Debtor's Plan, or at minimum obtain an increase commensurate with the shift in economic burden resulting from the tipping basket conversion.

E. Recommended Action

- Concede: Conversion of basket from deductible to tipping structure (per controlling deal instruction).
- Object: Reduction of the indemnification cap below the Debtor's Plan level.
- Counter-proposal: Restore the indemnification cap to the level in the Debtor's Plan, or increase the cap to reflect the additional burden placed on the estate/claimants by the tipping basket conversion. Confirm that all Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain covered by the indemnification regime.

---

IV. DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT (MAE) DEFINITION — REGULATORY ACTION CARVE-OUTS

A. Description of the Deviation

The Committee Plan amends the definition of Material Adverse Effect to add carve-outs for regulatory action — specifically, regulatory action of the same kind that is at issue in this restructuring. Under the Debtor's Plan, an MAE would be triggered by certain regulatory actions that have a material adverse impact on the debtor's business. The Committee Plan's carve-outs would exclude such regulatory actions from the definition of MAE, thereby preventing the estate/creditors from relying on them for the purposes of the MAE concept in the Plan.

B. Interaction with Schedule 3.7 (Pending Regulatory Inquiries)

Schedule 3.7 of the Debtor's Plan discloses two pending regulatory inquiries into the debtor's operations. These inquiries are of a character that would, under the Debtor's Plan's MAE definition, be treated as the kind of event that could constitute or contribute to a Material Adverse Effect. The Committee Plan's newly added carve-out for regulatory action is drafted to match precisely the type of regulatory action under investigation in those two pending inquiries.

By adding these carve-outs, the Committee Plan would have the effect of neutralizing the MAE trigger associated with the very regulatory inquiries that are already disclosed on Schedule 3.7. This is a substantive change that does more than simply clarify the scope of the MAE definition — it operates to strip the estate/creditors of a remedy for the specific regulatory risk already known and disclosed.

C. Valuation Assessment

The valuation summary assumes that the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 carry potential material exposure. The valuation projections incorporate the possibility that one or both inquiries could result in material adverse consequences. The MAE carve-outs proposed by the Committee would remove the contractual protection tied to these disclosed risks, without any corresponding adjustment to the consideration or value allocated under the Plan. In effect, the Committee Plan would shift regulatory risk back to the estate/claimants without compensation.

D. Negotiating Position

The MAE carve-out for regulatory action is not a point the client has conceded. The carve-outs directly intersect Schedule 3.7 disclosures and would neutralize the MAE protection for known, disclosed regulatory risks. This deviation should be rejected in its entirety.

E. Recommended Action

- Object: The addition of carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action of the kind at issue.
- Counter-proposal: Strike the carve-outs entirely, or, at minimum, limit any carve-out so that it does not apply to the two regulatory inquiries already disclosed on Schedule 3.7. If a carve-out is retained in any form, seek a compensating adjustment to the distribution waterfall or indemnification limits to reflect the transferred risk.

---

V. DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION

A. Description of the Deviation

The Committee Plan introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations relative to the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B to the Debtor's Plan. Under the Debtor's Plan, Exhibit B establishes the survival periods for each category of representation (e.g., fundamental reps, general reps, and specific indemnification-related reps). The Committee Plan's new limitation period would cut the survival period for the core representations short of what Exhibit B provides.

B. Interaction with Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)

Exhibit B is a controlling schedule that sets the survival matrix for representations and warranties under the Debtor's Plan. The scheduled exceptions in Exhibit B control over general statements in the base materials. The Committee Plan's limitation-period change directly contradicts Exhibit B.

The Committee's proposed reduction would mean that claims for breach of core representations would need to be brought within a shorter window after confirmation, even though (i) the parties had expressly negotiated the survival periods reflected in Exhibit B, and (ii) the debtor was aware that certain claims (including those tied to the Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries and Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities) may only become apparent after an extended period of time.

C. Valuation Assessment

The valuation summary and disclosure statement excerpts indicate that the survival periods in Exhibit B are materially linked to the recoveries contemplated under the Plan. Shortening the survival period would shorten the window during which the estate/creditors could pursue claims for misrepresentations, thereby reducing the effective value of the Plan's protections without any corresponding benefit to the estate.

D. Negotiating Position

Per the controlling deal correspondence, the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This is the highest-priority position in the negotiation. The client will not accept a reduction in the survival period for the core representations. This is a non-negotiable point.

E. Recommended Action

- Object: The reduction of any survival period below the levels in Exhibit B.
- Walk-away: If the Committee insists on the shortened survival period, the client has indicated this is a walk-away issue.
- Counter-proposal: Require that the survival periods for all core representations remain consistent with Exhibit B. No reduction in survival will be accepted.

---

VI. SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDED POSITIONS

| Deviation | Document Reference | Position | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a. Indemnification cap reduction | Schedule 5.2; Debtor's Plan §(indemnification) | Object — seek restoration | Silent reduction materially shifts value from estate/claimants; not conceded |
| 1b. Indemnity basket conversion (deductible → tipping) | Schedule 5.2; Debtor's Plan §(indemnification) | Concede | Controlling deal instruction concedes basket conversion |
| 2. MAE regulatory-action carve-outs | Schedule 3.7; Debtor's Plan §(MAE) | Object — strike or narrow | Carve-outs neutralize MAE for two disclosed pending regulatory inquiries |
| 3. Survival period reduction | Exhibit B; Debtor's Plan §(survival) | Object — walk-away position | Any survival reduction is a walk-away issue per controlling deal instruction; contradictions Exhibit B |

---

VII. CONCLUSION

The Committee Plan introduces three material deviations from the Debtor's Plan of Reorganization. Of these, the client has conceded the indemnity basket conversion. The remaining deviations — the indemnification cap reduction, the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs, and the survival period reduction — should be resolved as follows:

- The indemnification cap reduction should be resisted and restored to the Debtor's Plan level, with due regard to the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.
- The MAE carve-outs for regulatory action should be rejected or narrowly tailored so as not to eliminate MAE protection for the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.
- The survival period reduction should be rejected outright; any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue per the controlling client instruction.

The firm should communicate these positions to the committee promptly, noting the governing deal correspondence priorities. All three open deviations must be reconciled before this Plan is finalized.

---

Prepared by: Law Firm Company
Practice Area: Bankruptcy Restructuring
Deliverable: plan-deviation-report.docx
